Hunter — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and our recommended next steps so we can get a focused model-fit run on Redwood: 

1) Scope we heard: summarization of discharge notes + canonical coding suggestions for ACE-2 cohort. Target throughput: 300 reqs/min during peak tests; latency sensitivity under 350ms p95.
2) Success criteria (customer): ROUGE-L >= 0.72 on the summarization set; precision@10 for coding suggestions >= 0.86.
3) Data format: CSV with columns: patient_id, note_text, gold_summary, gold_codes. Sample attached (medlogic_sample_dataset_v1.csv).

Our immediate asks: could you send a 500–1k record sample (de-identified) following the attached sample format? Also confirm any sections you want removed from notes (PHI scrub rules).

Ben (cc'd) will own the Redwood eval runbook and scoring; Priyom will coordinate onboarding and SSO access.

Proposed timeline: we can run a first-fit pass within 72 hours of receiving the sample and evaluate on the scorecard. If that works, plan a 2-week benchmark with expanded data.

Next steps I can action: share the Redwood eval template, link to the model catalog recommendations, and spin up a temporary dedicated slot for the run. If that sounds right, I’ll kick off the access request and send the scoring rubric.

Thanks — Sean

Hi Hunter — thanks, Sean. Answering your two clarifying Qs and adding ops details so the evaluation is reproducible: 

1) Gold codes format: please send gold_codes as a JSON array string (e.g. ["I10","E11.9"]) in the gold_codes column. That maps cleanly into our scorer and preserves multiplicity.

2) Prompt templates: attached is a recommended prompt-set (prompt-set-v2.jsonl) with a short templating layer we use for summarization and code-suggestion. We include examples for temperature=0.0 (deterministic coding) and temperature=0.7 (exploratory summary).

Evaluation plan (high level):
- Baseline models to test: redwood-bison-7B (quantized int8) for cost/throughput; redwood-guardian-13B (float16) for quality baseline. We will also test redwood-guardian-13B with KV-cache warm-start for long notes.
- Scoring: we will run ROUGE-L and BERTScore for summaries; map gold_codes vs predicted_codes with precision/recall@k and a normalized partial-credit metric for hierarchical ICD groups.
- Regression guardrails: we will run prompt-set-heldout (50 examples) across every model variant and compute a rolling baseline. If ROUGE-L drops >0.03 or precision@5 drops >0.05 vs baseline, the system will flag a regression and we will auto-rollback to the last passing model.

Data handling & security: Redwood Private will ingest the sample into a customer-scoped bucket; we will apply automatic redaction hooks you confirm (e.g., remove tokens matching MRN patterns). We can also sign an NDA for the full benchmark dataset if needed.

Ops: attaching the Redwood eval template (redwood_eval_template.xlsx) — it contains the column mapping, scorer weights, and a checklist for pre-flight: sample size, de-id confirmation, and SSO user list. Once you drop the sample in the shared Drive link (see drive URL) I’ll schedule the first-fit run.

Estimated timings: first-fit pass (500–1k rows) in 48–72 hours after sample + SSO; full 2-week benchmark depends on final sample size and requested model variants.

If this plan looks right, please: 1) upload sample to the shared Drive link; 2) confirm de-id rules in a reply; 3) provide a list of 2–3 users who need access.

Thanks — Ben
